text:
incidentbot: PagerDuty alert: PD#INC-7331 fired -> eng-oncall (policy=latency-critical). symptom: router.p95 spike > 900ms for 90s, pattern: short bursts every ~30s. graph: https://metrics.internal/redwood/router/p95?start=1746023400

claire-oncall: I'm on it. did PD escalate or is this the first page?

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD#INC-7331 routed to eng-oncall. auto-escalate in 3m.

amir.ops: acked. pulling up proxy and host telemetry. quick check: any customer tickets?

rea-support: one customer slack message about slow dev env, no 5xxs reported. asked them to paste request ids.

de vin-runtime: initial traces show a hotspot: a single proxy pod (proxy-b-3) is handling a disproportionate number of long tail requests. TCP retransmit counts up on host node n-12.

claire-oncall: can we shift traffic off proxy-b-3? runbook suggests cordon+drain for noisy proxy.

amir.ops: executing: `kubectl get pods -l app=proxy -o wide | grep proxy-b-3` then `kubectl drain proxy-b-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=10`

devin-runtime: while that's happening, i've toggled per-pod circuit breaker to route new sessions away from proxy-b-3.

incidentbot: PagerDuty note: PD#INC-7331 acknowledged by amir.ops at 12:14:38.

rea-support: customer sent req ids: r=dev-77ff, dev-77gg. both show 4-6s latency then normal. thanking them for quick confirmation.

devin-runtime: host n-12 dmesg shows repeated PCIe AER errors around 12:14:20, likely NIC issues. also we see a scheduling hiccup on gpu host that caused temp kernel stall. pushing a live host-driver reload: `systemctl restart network-driver`

amir.ops: driver restart done, interrupts drop. LB now shows even distribution across proxy pods. p95 back to ~140ms. https://metrics.internal/redwood/router/p95?range=10m

claire-oncall: nice. PD will auto-resolve if alert clears. i'll keep monitoring for 5 more mins.

devin-runtime: one oddity: KV cache miss rate spiked briefly during the reroute, likely due to session affinity change. normalized within 30s.

amir.ops: creating follow-up INF ticket INF-1959: "n-12 PCIe/NIC AER events causing transient router latency" and assigning to eng-infra.

paging note: this looks like a flapping pattern caused by transient host noise, not application regression. recommend we add a short suppression window for router p95 alerts when single-host NIC errors detected.

claire-oncall: action items: 1) infra to inspect NIC firmware and chassis logs for n-12, 2) add temporary alert suppression rule (30s grace) for router.p95 when host-level pci/aer events detected, 3) update runbook to include quick driver reload and immediate cordon+drain steps. tagging infra and runtime.

rea-support: i'll update customer message: brief transient slowdown, no sustained errors, we're opening infra ticket and will follow up. include request ids.

devin-runtime: also adding a small ephemeral metric to fire earlier for NIC AER counts so we can preemptively quarantine a host before router.p95 trips.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD#INC-7331 auto-resolved at 12:18:40 (no escalation).

claire-oncall: marking customer-impact low and transient. opening a short RCA note in INF-1959 and will link to this thread.

amir.ops: thumbs up. lessons: our current p95 threshold was doing its job catching the blip but produced a noisy page that resolved quickly. let's tune to avoid repeat chatter for single-host hardware noise. :white_check_mark:

rea-support: customers notified. no followups required now.

claire-oncall: closing thread at 12:22. thanks folks. :pray:
